programme: DDIT3 (CHOP), the terminal transcription factor of the PERK/ATF4 integrated stress response, sits at the hub of a stress-to-inflammation relay together with RELA (NF-κB p65) and the AP-1 factor FOSL1, which carry ER-stress signaling into inflammatory and apoptotic gene induction; LRRFIP1 feeds the same relay from upstream as a cytosolic nucleic-acid/danger sensor that also converges on NF-κB-linked signaling. This is a transcriptional stress relay, not a stable bound complex.
role_in_a: In bipolar disorder, lymphoblastoid cells from patients show an aberrant ER-stress response running through DDIT3/CHOP (consistent with the mitochondrial/ER-stress hypothesis of BD), LRRFIP1 carries a GWAS signal for BD/schizophrenia, and FOSL1-linked transcriptomic changes (including an altered IL-17 axis) are reported in BD patient transcriptomes.
role_in_b: In stroke, ischemia-reperfusion drives an ER-stress/UPR programme in which DDIT3 is identified among the key stress and hypoxia/immune biomarker genes, RELA/NF-κB is a central documented driver of post-ischemic neuroinflammation, LRRFIP1 appears in the DAPK1 interactome of neurons exposed to ischemic-like insult, and FOSL1 is implicated in endothelial metabolic stress shared with cerebrovascular injury.
shared_axis: Both conditions involve cellular stress states — chronic ER/mitochondrial stress in bipolar disorder's affected blood and neural cells, acute ischemic/oxidative stress in stroke — that can converge on the same PERK-DDIT3 branch feeding NF-κB (RELA) and AP-1 (FOSL1) transcription, with LRRFIP1 as a shared upstream sensor; recurrence of this module across a blood-network and a brain-network is consistent with a common stress-response circuit rather than a stroke- or BD-specific pathway.
reasoning: Three of the four carrying factors (DDIT3, FOSL1, LRRFIP1) have direct, disease-specific PMIDs in both bipolar disorder and stroke independently, and the module is nameable as a recognized ER-stress/NF-κB-AP-1 relay, which argues against 'insufficient'. But no retrieved paper ties bipolar disorder and stroke together through this axis (RELA's BD link is only an Open Targets score, no supporting text), so the cross-disease connection itself rests on inference from parallel, disease-separate evidence rather than a stated shared fact.
support: PMID 18771604 shows aberrant ER-stress response (DDIT3/CHOP pathway) in bipolar disorder lymphoblastoid cells; PMID 38942324 identifies DDIT3 among ER-stress genes in ischemic stroke; PMID 38384585 places DDIT3-related hypoxia/immune biomarkers in ischemic stroke; PMID 40539026 shows FOSL1-linked IL-17 pathway alteration in bipolar disorder transcriptomes; PMID 40727846 places FOSL1 in a bipolar/schizophrenia/MDD transcriptomic signature; PMID 37775708 implicates FOSL1 in shared endothelial metabolic stress in stroke and Alzheimer's disease; PMID 31096178 is a GWAS review supporting LRRFIP1 in bipolar disorder/schizophrenia; PMID 33265962 places LRRFIP1 in the DAPK1 interactome of neurons under ischemic-like stress; PMID 42621097 shows RELA/NF-κB signaling driving stroke progression; PMID 42196418 places RELA among inflammatory response genes in ischemic stroke.
how_to_falsify: In bipolar-disorder patient-derived lymphoblastoid or iPSC-neuron lines and in an ischemia-reperfusion (OGD) neuronal/endothelial model, block the PERK-ATF4-DDIT3 arm (e.g., PERK inhibitor or DDIT3 knockdown) and measure RELA- and FOSL1-target induction (IL6, CXCL8, MMP9); if NF-κB/AP-1 target induction under stress is unchanged in both systems, the proposed DDIT3-to-RELA/FOSL1 relay is not the operative link and the account is wrong.
caveats: The comparison is cross-tissue (blood-derived networks for bipolar disorder vs. brain/vascular networks for stroke), and rests on only 15 patient-group comparisons drawn from 4 independent cohort pairs, with these factors concordant in 11-12 of 15 rather than all. Several other concordant factors (BRCA1, SOX17, SOX4, GLI1, TCF20, MYB, FOXJ1, RXRA) were deliberately excluded from the programme because they represent separate biology (DNA repair, endothelial/ciliary development, hedgehog and nuclear-receptor signaling) that does not mechanistically join the stress-inflammation relay — their presence may instead reflect tissue composition rather than shared disease process. FOS, an AP-1 partner that would fit this story neatly, was excluded as single-view (recurrence 0.53) and is correctly left out. The tissue-generic removal list already strips out several blood/immune TFs (CEBPB, CEBPD, NFATC1, etc.), which is why DDIT3/RELA/FOSL1/LRRFIP1 surviving that filter is more informative than if no filtering had occurred.
